title: Inputs and outputs
summary: Digital signals in and out: how a button becomes TRUE in the program and how TRUE in the program switches a lamp.
objectives: Read a digital input in a program
Explain what the input LED shows

sections.heading: TRUE and FALSE
sections.body: A digital input reads a voltage: 24 V means **TRUE**, 0 V means **FALSE**. A digital output switches 24 V to a load when the program sets it **TRUE**. In PLC Lab each signal has a name (a **tag**) such as `Button1` or `Lamp1`.

sections.heading: From terminal to tag
sections.body: The I/O module converts the voltage at a terminal into a bit in the input image; your program reads the tag mapped to that bit.
sections.diagram:
button --24V--> [DI terminal 0] --LED--> input image bit --> tag Button1
  tag Lamp1 --> output image bit --> [DO terminal 0] --24V--> lamp

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Writing the assignment the wrong way round (`Button1 := Lamp1;`) does not compile: inputs are read-only in the program. The PLC Lab compiler tells you exactly that.

sections.heading: Predict
sections.body: Look at the example and predict.

question.question: Button1 is pressed and held. What is Lamp1 in the next scan?
question.explanation: The assignment copies the input value into the output every scan.

sections.heading: Practice: pushbutton and lamp
sections.body: Write the program, then press **Build & Load to PLC**: it compiles the program, loads it into the simulated PLC, sets the PLC mode switch to RUN and starts the simulation. The toolbar has two separate controls. **PLC RUN / STOP** is the PLC's mode switch: in RUN the program executes once in every PLC cycle; in STOP it does not execute and the outputs go to their stop state (normally off), while the machine itself keeps running. **Simulation Run / Pause / Step / Stop** controls the simulated world: Run lets time pass (the machine moves and, in RUN, the PLC scans every cycle), Pause freezes everything, Step advances exactly one PLC cycle, and Stop restores the machine's initial state while the PLC keeps its program. Then press S1 in the Process view and watch the cause-and-effect panel.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Inputs become TRUE/FALSE tags; assigning a tag to an output switches the output.

**Troubleshooting note:** If a lamp does not light, compare the output tag, the output LED and the lamp: they tell you whether the program, the module or the field wiring is at fault.

checkpoint.question: What does an input LED show?
options: The electrical state at the terminal
checkpoint.explanation: The LED is driven by the input circuit, before the program.

checkpoint.question: Which statement writes an output?
checkpoint.explanation: ':=' assigns the right side to the left side.
